title: A Shifting Perspective: How "Malèna" Makes Us Confront Our Own Gaze

commenti.body:
The movie shows us all the bad things that comes with the objectification of Malena, how she is only seen and used for her beauty by the townspeople, including Renato. It is a smart way of telling a story because the protagonist is a part of the problem in the begining, but starts to see Malena as a person in the end and he grows as a character. 

I believe it is easy to missinterpret the movie as being a part of the  ''male gaze'' and promoting sexualization. Yes, it shows us the ''male gaze'', but the movie examines it to the core and problematizes the gaze. The film shows us why it is bad to only see a woman for her looks and not her personality and accomplishments. Great film.

Completely agree. The film doesn’t promote the male gaze but instead critiques it. It makes us realize how harmful it is to reduce a woman to just her appearance. Renato's growth is key to that message. It’s powerful storytelling. (mod: r/NetflixByProxy)

I don't know about all that, but I think it definitely is somewhat of a sexploitation (?) film rather than an indictment that's 'confronting the male gaze.' Sometimes a cigar is just a cigar. And sorry to be crass but Monica Belucci is so very hot in this movie, particularly the uncensored original cut where she's on display in all her hairy glory. I can see the more modest Weinstein cut seeming more tactful but the original is pretty clear cut about its intentions.

Uhhhhh sounds like the worst thing to happen to her is due to the violent jealousy of other women, and not the pesky men and their gazes who then don't interfere in the beatings out of respect for / deference to their wives.

Wtf I remember running into that beating scene on YT years ago and pretty sure that wasn't Belucci? I would've recognized her??

Fucking Mandela man. OR maybe there's several movies with scenes like this, or it's a remake / different adaptation / who knows?  
Need to go look into that
the film would have zero reason to exist as a story without the themes that the OP explored here.
